key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows different solid-state conversion routes in wide- and narrow-bandgap perovskites, so bandgap control depends on stack-specific chemistry rather than a single deposition recipe.
engineering_relevance: This enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandems with tuned absorber bandgaps, culminating in a 19.2% efficient device and improved thermal stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare conversion pathways in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Tune absorber bandgap via precursor thickness and annealing control
evidence_signal: The study reports absorbers spanning 1.26–1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem with 19.2% efficiency, and 80% average retained efficiency after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and chemistry-dependent conversion mean process windows may be narrow, especially for reproducible large-area scaling.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
